core_obligations: Construct f by first fixing z and getting a bilinear map out of M times N, then assembling the result into a bilinear map out of the tensor product with P (proof lines 2054-2065).
Construct the inverse h from the trilinear map M times N times P and check on pure tensors that the two composites are identities (proof lines 2066-2075).
proof_roadmap: Build one map by two applications of the universal property (proof lines 2053-2065).
Build its inverse from a trilinear pairing and compare on generators (proof lines 2066-2077).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the two displayed maps between (M tensor N) tensor P, the triple tensor product and M tensor (N tensor P) are well defined and isomorphisms (statement lines 2039-2051). The proof does not quote the associativity of the tensor product: it constructs the first map by fixing the third variable and applying bilinearity twice, constructs the inverse from the trilinear map on triples, and verifies the composites are identities by evaluating on pure tensors (proof lines 2053-2077). Deciding to peel off one variable at a time, so that only bilinearity is ever needed, is the content. H2.
